correctness.rationale: Finite exact theorem. Full 945-tree census independently generated by recursive binary hierarchies and repeated edge insertion; each of 105 quartet indicators independently checked by split cuts and four-point distances. Canonical-query exhaustive DFS enumerated 206,992 shattered prefixes; its extension iff all trace cells split is a proved characterization, sorted traversal is complete by hereditary shattering, and query transitivity proves coefficient double-counting. Independent witness data covers every one of 64 patterns for a six-query shattered support. Complete 504-support extremal orbit census under 5040 permutations gives sizes 1260,2520,5040. Python standard-library CHECKER.py was executed successfully from the included package path.

value.rationale: Determines all sizes of seven-leaf binary resolved-quartet shattering supports, the exact VC rank six, and all three symmetry types of its extremal six-query supports. This is a natural fixed-order calibration for phylogenetic quartet data and a nontrivial distinction between binary one-versus-rest learning and multiclass quartet Natarajan learning. VC increases 1,2,3,6 from four to seven taxa, so the jump at seven is a meaningful finite boundary rather than an arbitrary slice. No new general-n theorem is claimed.
